In the instant writ petition, the present petitioners claim relief for a lapsing declaration being made in terms of Section 24 (2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (herein after referred to as ' the Act of 2013').

sentences.text: Initially stated, the husband of the present writ-petitioner No.1 had filed CWP No. 3959-1992 and on the said writ petition, a verdict of dismissal (Annexure P-8) was made.

The aggrieved therefrom,
the husband 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086806-DB -
of the present petitioner No. 1 filed SLP bearing (Civil) No (s) 16814-2011 before Hon'ble the Supreme Court, whereons, the hereinfter extracted verdict was passed (Annexure P-9):-
"

After making some submissions, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner made a request that his client may be permitted to withdraw the special leave petition with liberty to seek review of the order under challenge by pointing out that some of the facts and material produced before the High Court had not been considered.
The request of the learned senior counsel is accepted and the special leave petition is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty in terms of the prayer made.

However, it is made clear that liberty given to the petitioner to file review petition shall not be construed as a mandate of this Court to the High Court to entertain the review petition and if any such petition is filed, the High Court shall decide the same on its own merits.
3.
Pursuant to the verdict (supra) being made on the afore SLP, thus a review petition became filed but the same became dismissed by this Court, vide order dated 14.10.2011 (Annexure P-10).

4. It appears that since the provisions of Section 24 (2) became inserted in the Act of 2013, thus, therebys, the instant writ petition has been raised before this Court by the petitioners wherebys they claim the making of a lapsing declaration in terms of Section 24 (2) of the Act of 2013.

5. sentences.text: In sequel, the espousal made by the present petitioners for the making a declaration in terms of Section 24 (2) of the Act of 2013 rather is rejected.

"5. That it is respectfully submitted that the notification u/s 4 of the Act was issued on 20.4.1990 for acquiring 1148.91 acres Acre (including the land in question of the petitioners) situated in the revenue estates of village Jharsa, Kanhai, Bindapur,
Samaspur Tehsil& District Gurugram.
The land measuring 475.51 acre of village Jharsa, 579.81 acre of Kanhai, 43.81 acre of Bindapur, 49.78 acre of Village Samaspur.
It was published in the local daily newspaper Veer Arjun (Hindi) on 24.4.1990 & The Statesman (English) on 27.4.1990.

Thereafter, munadi was also made in the locality by beating of drums and a report to this effect was also made which was reduced into writing and was also pasted at various places such as office of DRO, LAC, Gurugram, halka patwari office and various public places in the locality.

The substance of notification u/s 4 was also entered in the Patwari Rapat Rojnamacha Vakayati (MustriMunadi) vide Rapat no. 512 dated 30.4.1990 of village Kanhai, Tehsil & District Gurugram."
6.

Now coming to the plea of the respondents discriminating against the present petitioners, as purportedly arising from the respondents releasing the lands of similarly situated land owners,
whereas, the acquiring 3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086806-DB -
authority ommitting to release the subject lands, rather is concerned, hence this Court is of the view that even the said ground cannot be accepted by this Court.

7. The said inference becomes sparked from a perusal of para No. 28 of the reply on affidavit, para whereof is extracted hereinafter, perusal whereof reveals, that similarly situated persons had challenged the acquisition proceedings on the ground of discrimination, and, the said raised ground became rejected by this Court vide order dated 22.11.2020.

"28. That it is respectfully submitted that recently the similarly situated person had challenged the acquisition proceedings arising out of the same notifications agitating the similar grounds in CWP no. 20284 of 2020 which has been dismissed vide order dated 22.11.2020 with following observations:
'
.....Admittedly, the acquisition proceedings stood concluded for the land in question on 23.03.1993, when award was passed and petitioners withdrew the compensation for the land in question.
It is also not in dispute that possession of the land was taken on 23.03.1993 and the same stood reflected in the revenue record as a rapat to this effect was sanctioned.
Meaning thereby, all the ingredients of completing an acquisition were fulfilled in the year 1993 itself and the petitioners were also satisfied.

sentences.text: 3 On the contrary, it is some of the other landholders of the village who challenged the acquisition proceedings in the year 1992 by filing CWP No. 6129 of 1992 and 7079 of 1992.

These writ petitions were allowed on 18.01.2011 and on the basis of this order,
their land was ordered to be released vide documents Annexure P-12 to P-14.
Thus, it is clear that the circumstances leading to release of land of other landholders and present petitioners are different.

Similarly, the release order of Mahender Singh (P-17) is also of no help to petitioners as the land was released in that case on account of order passed by this Court in view of Section 24(2) of the Act,
2013 as interpreted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pune Municipal Corporation Vs Harak chand Misirimal 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086806-DB -
Solanki (2014(1) CTC 755).

entities.text: Pune Municipal Corporation Vs Harak chand Misirimal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, we fail to see how Section 24(2) would be applicable to petitioners even at that point of time, as petitioners had received the compensation and possession was also not with them, atleast in the official documents.

Be that as it may, the writ petition filed by father of petitioners bearing CWP No. 5339 of 2014 claiming release of land on the strength of section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 also stands dismissed by this Court on 17.11.2020 in view of the latest judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority's case (supra) and therefore the petitioners cannot claim parity with the said order as well.

Even in the present case the petitioners case cannot be considered under section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 as the possession stands taken and the compensation is duly tendered and further as far as plea of discrimination is concerned, the subject matter has been dealt with by the Co-ordinate bench in CWP no. 20284 of 2020 and thus the present case is squarely covered by the same."
8.

Consequently, if the ground of discrimination, as became earlier raised by some of the land losers concerned, who became aggrieved from the acquisition notification common to the petitioners therein vis-a-vis the petitioners before this Court, thus became rejected.
Therefore, the ground of discrimination as such raised even before this Court by the present petitioners is liable to be rejected.

The said reason becomes prima facie grooved in the premise, that when qua the apposite similarity of ground(supra), when became earlier pleaded and besides becomes rejected in the writ petitions (supra), therefore, the present petitioners become estopped to re-agitate the said ground of discrimination, even in the instant writ petition.

9. Be that as it may, most conspicuously since the husband of the petitioner no. 1, had earlier filed writ petition before this Court, whereons, a binding and conclusive verdict of dismissal was made.

Moreover, 5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086806-DB -
reiteratedly when the plea of discrimination as raised thereins became rejected, therebys the present petitioner No. 1 who is the wife of the erstwhile petitioner No. 1 also thereby becomes estopped to re-plead the said earlier raised rejected grounds.
